report.summary:
（重启的 WORLD 代理已完成：区块流式加载、Worker 池、编辑重建网格、方块更新、随机刻和 IndexedDB 存档都已实现，测试和浏览器验证全部通过。）

I restarted the WORLD role and finished it. All six owned modules are implemented to SPEC §8 / §9.6 and to the real code of the finished modules. Nothing is stubbed.

What each module does:
- **workerpool.js**: module workers. Jobs wait in a binary min-heap ordered by priority, then submission order. Each worker has at most 2 jobs in flight and gets jobs least-loaded first. It supports cancel and reprioritize. Error replies reject the job. A crashed worker (for example, its module fails to load) has its jobs rejected and is restarted up to 3 times with the last init replayed. terminate() rejects everything.
- **worker.js**: follows the §8 protocol, using WorldGenerator, then buildRegion → computeLight → meshChunk with getTints. Region and light buffers are reused between jobs. The message handler is exported so Node tests can run real jobs.
- **world.js**:
  - **Streaming:** loads the nearest chunks first. The mesh set is every chunk touching the 16·rd-block circle, so nothing visible before the fog ends is missing. The generation set is its 3×3 neighbourhood (≈ rd+1); chunks are unloaded beyond one more ring (≈ rd+2). Saved chunks load from Storage before anything is generated.
  - **Jobs:** generation jobs are queued all at once, reprioritized as the player moves, and cancelled when their chunk unloads. Mesh jobs are throttled. They send only the block layers up to each chunk's highest block, in pooled buffers the worker sends back.
  - **Edits** follow §9.6: every chunk within ±15 blocks gets sections 0..(y+15)>>4 marked dirty. The chunks touching the 3×3×3 cube around the edit are meshed first as one group, and the group is uploaded in a single frame, so there are no holes at chunk borders. Every job carries a global edit counter and each section remembers the newest result, so out-of-order or racing results never lose an edit.
  - **Uploads** are limited to about 4 ms per frame, nearest first. A section whose 53-bit mesh hash hasn't changed is not uploaded again.
  - **Lighting and heightmaps:** light is stored trimmed (5.2 MB instead of 15.1 MB at rd 8, exact). Heightmaps back getTopY. isAreaReady takes block coordinates.
  - **Random ticks:** grass spreads to lit dirt and turns to dirt under opaque blocks or liquid. Saplings grow through a main-thread generator.growTree. Sugar cane and cactus grow up to 3 tall, and ice melts next to torches.
  - **Saving:** save() writes 16 chunks per transaction. A modified chunk that unloads goes into a save buffer that is checked again on reload, so edits survive even with storage = null. destroy() saves first.
- **blockupdates.js**: a queue-based processor, no recursion. Blocks that lose their support pop off and drop their loot, cascading upward. Sand and gravel fall instantly to the landing cell, replacing water or short grass, or breaking into an item on a torch or flower. An optional hook can hand them to entities.js falling-block entities instead.
- **storage.js**: IndexedDB `webcraft` with `worlds` and `chunks` stores. Chunk keys are [worldId, cx, cz], so deleteWorld removes a key range in one transaction. Reads issued together share one transaction. If IndexedDB is unavailable it falls back to memory with a single console warning. rleEncode/rleDecode use a varint run-length format: a 64 KB surface chunk becomes about 4–12 KB, and corrupt data throws a RangeError.

Measured in headless Edge with the RTX 4070 and 8 workers:
- **rd 8:** 313 chunks loaded and 241 meshed in about 370 ms; the spawn area (radius 2) is ready in about 165 ms.
- **rd 16:** 1013 chunks loaded and 877 meshed in 844 ms.
- **Main thread:** world.update() costs at most 4.1 ms per frame, and no frame took over 50 ms.
- **Edits:** a block edit is on the GPU in the next frame (16.7 ms); the worker result is back in about 4.7 ms. A 4096-block /fill is remeshed and uploaded in about 30 ms.
- **Flying:** at 30 and 60 blocks/s the player's area was never unready, and update() stayed at or under 1.3 ms.
- **Persistence:** about 9,850 edited cells survived an in-page reload and a real page reload from IndexedDB, and also flying away and coming back.
apiDeviations: Additive constructor options for World: onFallingBlock(blockId, x, y, z) -> bool (return true after spawning a falling-block entity; otherwise blocks fall instantly per wave 1), uploadBudgetMs (default 4), tickRadius (default 8), maxMeshJobs, generator. onDropItem and onFallingBlock are also settable properties.
tick(rng, timeOfDay) takes an optional second argument. Sky light for growth rules is reduced by skyLightLevelAt(timeOfDay); without it, sky light counts as full daylight.

onBlockChanged(fn) returns an unsubscribe function. stats() adds idle, uploadQueue, jobs, renderDistance, generated, avgGenerateMs, loadedFromStorage, meshJobs, avgMeshMs, uploads, uploadsSkipped and uploadMB.

Extra World members: world.generator (main-thread WorldGenerator, created on first use), getBiome(x, z), findSpawn() -> {x, y, z}, getChunk(cx, cz) (debug), plus seed / worldType / worldId / renderDistance / smoothLighting / persistent fields.

Streaming radii are defined geometrically. The mesh set is every chunk intersecting the circle of radius 16·rd blocks, slightly more than 'centre distance <= rd', so the fog edge never shows missing chunks. The generation set is its 3×3 neighbourhood (~rd+1) and chunks unload outside the 5×5 neighbourhood (~beyond rd+2).

Additive worker protocol fields: mesh jobs may send trimmed chunk copies (whole 256-byte layers; missing top layers are air) plus returnBuffers and trimLight flags. 'meshed' replies add hash per section, ms and buffers; with trimLight the light array only covers the region's highest block + 15 (everything above is exactly 0xF0). Plain spec messages with full chunks still work and get full 65536-byte light.
getLight returns 0xF0 for unknown cells and also for cells below the world (y < 0), not only above it.

WorkerPool: an extra options argument { maxInFlight = 2, createWorker } (for tests), size / queued / inFlight / liveWorkers / getStats(), and exported JobCancelledError and defaultWorkerCount(). Cancelled jobs reject with an AbortError whose cancelled === true.

Storage: Storage.open({ name, indexedDB }) never rejects. Additions: Storage.memory(), persistent, backend, close(), encodeChunkRecord/decodeChunkRecord, newWorldId(). rleDecode(u8, length) may be called without a length. saveChunks compresses the block arrays synchronously during the call.
setBlock with the block's current id returns true with no side effects. Ids that are not valid blocks return false, and a world that is being destroyed rejects edits.
report.tests:
Node: `node --test tests/world.test.js tests/storage.test.js` gives 42 of 42 passing in about 1.5 s. The full suite, `node --test "tests/*.test.js"`, gives 304 of 304 passing.
- `tests/world.test.js` (33 tests): chunk keys, heightmaps, dirty ranges, invariants of the loading sets (every visible chunk is meshed and every mesh chunk's neighbours are generated), circular order, block updates (popping, gravity, falling out of the world, budget, falling-entity hook), worker protocol, and the WorkerPool with fake workers.
- The same file also drives the World end-to-end with a fake pool that runs the real worker code. This covers loading order, block queries, edit priorities and groups, racing and out-of-order results, unload/save/restore with and without storage, save followed by a new World instance, random ticks, tree growth, ice, smooth-lighting changes, the context-loss remesh, render-distance changes, job cancellation on teleport, failure fallbacks and an unavailable storage index.
- Every meshed section of a default-terrain world is compared word for word against a direct meshChunk of the world data, and getLight is compared against a direct computeLight for all 65,536 cells of a chunk.
- `tests/storage.test.js` (9 tests): RLE edge cases, varint boundaries, random and real chunk data, corrupt input, and the in-memory Storage (CRUD, ordering, deleteWorld isolation, fallback warning).

Browser, all runs ended with no page errors:
- `node tools/harness.mjs --url "tools/world-test.html?rd=8" --wait-for window.__done` (also run with rd=12/16 and render=1): IndexedDB self-test, load timings, edit latency, bulk edits, save, in-page reload, fast flight and verification of about 9,850 edited cells.
- `--steps tools/world-steps.json`: a real page reload, after which phase 2 reopens the world from IndexedDB with 9850 of 9850 edits present.
- `?render=1 --steps tools/world-shots.json` writes tools/out/world-monument.png, world-overview.png, world-hole.png, world-monument-night.png and world-monument-flat.png, which I inspected visually (plus world-lightdiff.png, a smooth vs flat difference heat-map showing the AO halos).
- `tools/world-pool-test.html`: 19 of 19 checks with real module workers, including a worker module that fails to load.
knownIssues: Liquids do not flow (there is no fluid simulation). Digging next to a lake leaves a vertical wall of water, and sand removed from under water leaves an air pocket.

Cactus is not broken by solid blocks beside it, and sugar cane does not require water. The shared hasSupport (which interaction.js also uses for placement) is the only rule, so a block the player was allowed to place never pops off immediately.
Saplings, sugar cane and cactus have no growth stages, so growth uses equivalent probabilities (1/14 for saplings, 1/16 for cane and cactus) with Minecraft's average timing.
Block arrays are a fixed 64 KB per loaded chunk (about 20 MB at rd 8, 65 MB at rd 16). Light is stored trimmed.
Only one World per WorkerPool at a time: call destroy() on the old world before init() of the next one on the shared pool.
IndexedDB writes started while a tab closes may not finish. Autosave plus saving on visibilitychange (hidden), which the spec already requires, covers this.
report.integrationNotes:
Wiring in main.js / game.js (more detail in docs/notes/world.md):

- **Create once:** `storage = await Storage.open()` and `pool = new WorkerPool()`, shared by all worlds.
- **startWorld(meta):**
  - Construct `world = new World({ seed: meta.seed, worldType: meta.worldType, worldId: meta.id, storage /* or null for unsaved autostart worlds */, pool, renderer, renderDistance: settings.renderDistance, smoothLighting: settings.smoothLighting, onDropItem: (id, n, x, y, z) => game.spawnItem(makeStack(id, n), x, y - 0.25, z), onFallingBlock: (id, x, y, z) => !!game.entities?.spawnFallingBlock(id, x + 0.5, y, z + 0.5) })`. onDropItem receives the block centre; the onFallingBlock line is optional and gives Minecraft-style falling sand through entities.js.
  - Then `await world.init()`; it calls pool.init(seed, worldType) itself.
- **New worlds:** `const sp = world.findSpawn(); meta.spawn = { x: sp.x + 0.5, y: sp.y, z: sp.z + 0.5 }`.
- **Loading screen:** call world.update(spawn.x, spawn.y, spawn.z, dt) every frame until `world.isAreaReady(spawn.x, spawn.z, 2)`. That function takes block coordinates, as player.js uses it, and ignores chunks outside the render distance. For progress use world.stats().meshed against loaded. You can raise world.uploadBudgetMs (for example to 12) during loading and set it back to 4 afterwards.
- **Frame order:** player.update, interaction.update, ticks, entities, then world.update(player.x, player.y, player.z, dt), then render. Edits made before world.update show up in the next frame.
- **Ticks:** `world.tick(rng, game.timeOfDay)` at 20 TPS. The timeOfDay argument is optional and dims sky light at night for growth rules.
- **Events and callbacks:**
  - `world.onBlockChanged((x, y, z, o, n) => game.emit('blockChanged', x, y, z, o, n))`.
  - `renderer.onContextRestored = () => game.world?.remeshAll()`. This is required, because uploads are skipped while the WebGL context is lost.
  - On settingsChanged: `world.setRenderDistance(s.renderDistance)` and `world.setSmoothLighting(s.smoothLighting)`.
- **Saving and quitting:** autosave and visibilitychange call `await world.save()` plus storage.saveWorldMeta(meta). quitToTitle should `await world.destroy()` (it saves, cancels jobs and removes meshes) before the next world starts on the same pool. If destroy rejects, the data is kept and save() can be retried.
- **Debug:** game.debug.waitIdle can poll `world.stats().idle`. For F3 use world.stats() and `world.getBiome(x, z).displayName`. /seed can read world.seed (commands.js already falls back to ctx.world.seed).
- **Worlds list:** game.listWorlds, deleteWorld and createWorld map directly to storage.listWorlds(), storage.deleteWorld(id), and storage.saveWorldMeta(meta) with `newWorldId()` from storage.js for the id.

report.summary:
重启后的音频 agent 已完成全部工作（上一次尝试因 API 限流在写代码前中断）。This is the restarted audio agent and the work is complete. src/game/audio.js implements SPEC §9.9 entirely with WebAudio synthesis; there are no audio files.

Architecture:
- `SoundCore` holds the mixer, voices, positional audio and the music scheduler. It works on any BaseAudioContext, so the same code renders into an OfflineAudioContext for the self-check.
- `AudioEngine` is the public API. It creates the AudioContext lazily on the first user gesture, does nothing before unlock, and never throws (also when WebAudio is missing or the context constructor throws).

Building blocks:
- Cached white, pink and brown noise buffers (3 s, seamless loops).
- Envelopes, filter sweeps and oscillator glides.
- Formant voices: sawtooth sources through bandpass formants with vibrato, growl modulation and breath noise.
- "Grain clouds": dozens of crunchy grains made with one noise source, one filter and one gain curve.
- Two generated reverb impulses on send buses: a short room for sound effects and a long hall for music.
- Sound and music sub-buses, an underwater lowpass and a soft limiter.
- A voice limiter (24 voices, the oldest is faded out in 25 ms), a spam guard (at most 3 identical sounds per 35 ms), and random pitch, level (±10 %) and recipe details on every play.

Block sounds work like Minecraft's SoundType: each material has a dig recipe (break and place at pitch 0.8) and a step recipe (step; hit at pitch 0.5; land at pitch 0.75 plus a thud). All 10 materials are covered: crunchy stone, a hollow multi-mode wood knock, grainy gravel, high-passed grass rustle, soft sand, glass shatter with sine pings, muffled wool, squeaky snow, bright metal clank, and water as bucket fill/pour with bubbles.

Named sounds: all 18 from the spec plus two extras, `ignite` and `fizz`.

Positional audio uses Minecraft's linear falloff (16-block range, 64 for explosions; volume above 1 extends the range). Panning is relative to the listener yaw in the SPEC §4 convention, and sounds behind or far away are slightly darker. Long sounds re-pan as the listener moves.

Loudness was calibrated with tools/audio-calibrate.mjs, which measures the loudest 100 ms (A-weighted) of each sound. The resulting per-material/per-kind trims are in `BLOCK_TRIM_DB` and per-sound gains in `SOUNDS[name].gain`.

Music:
- The generative composer is pure and seeded. It picks a mode (major, lydian, aeolian, dorian or mixolydian), a curated maj7/add9 chord progression, and a style (Wet Hands-like arpeggio, block chords, pulse, sparse or waltz). Form: intro → A → B → A → rolled final chord with ritardando. Melodies repeat and vary a motif, and phrases are separated by rests.
- The piano is additive synthesis: inharmonic partials, two-stage decay from detuned unison strings, and hammer noise. Notes are rendered once per 3 semitones in an OfflineAudioContext, so the work happens off the main thread, then replayed with velocity-dependent brightness and a damper at note-off.
- Scheduling looks ahead 1 s. The first piece starts 3–9 s after `startMusic()`, then 1.5–4 minutes of silence separate pieces, and `stopMusic()` fades out. After a hitch the piece slides forward instead of bursting or dropping notes.

I could not listen to anything in headless mode; sounds were checked through spectrograms and loudness measurements only.
apiDeviations: All changes are additive; no SPEC signature is broken.

`new AudioEngine(settings, options?)` takes an optional second argument: { maxVoices = 24, autoUnlock = true (its own window gesture listeners call unlock), suspendWhenHidden = true, AudioContextClass (for tests), seed, force }.

`play()` and `playBlock()` return a voice handle { stop(fade), setPosition(x, y, z), playing }, or null when nothing was played (unknown name, inaudible, not unlocked yet, muted). The SPEC does not define a return value.
`playBlock(kind, material, x, y, z, opts?)` accepts an optional { volume, pitch }. An unknown material falls back to 'stone'; an unknown kind returns null.
`play()` volume above 1 extends the audible range (16 blocks × volume) with gain capped at 1, as in Minecraft. Omitting x/y/z gives a centred, non-positional sound.
`setVolumes()` with no arguments re-reads settings.soundVolume / settings.musicVolume from the constructor's settings object.
`startMusic({ delay })` and `stopMusic({ fade })` take optional options. `unlock()` returns a boolean.
Extra methods: setUnderwater(bool), playMusicNow(seed?), plus `musicStatus`, `unlocked` and `available` getters and `destroy()`.
Extra sound names: 'ignite' (flint and steel) and 'fizz' (water on lava / extinguishing).

Extra exports for tests and tools: SoundCore, SynthKit, SOUND_NAMES, BLOCK_KINDS, BLOCK_MATERIALS, composePiece, pieceMidis, ensurePianoSamples, makeNoise, makeImpulse, spatialize, analyzeBuffer, renderSoundOffline, renderMusicOffline, and mulberry32 (re-exported from util/noise.js).
report.tests:
Unit tests: `node --test tests/audio.test.js` passes 18/18. They use a strict mock AudioContext that throws on the same misuse real WebAudio does (non-finite or negative times, exponential ramp to 0, starting a source twice, stop before start, overlapping value curves, invalid filter/oscillator types, wrong convolver buffers) and checks that every source is started, stopped and reaches the destination. Coverage:
- Noise colours and seamless loop; reverb impulse decay and left/right decorrelation.
- Positional audio against the SPEC yaw convention: range, linear falloff, panning, darker sounds behind.
- Composer over 60 seeds: deterministic, all notes in key, sorted, value ranges, density.
- Every named sound and every kind×material combination.
- Voice stealing, spam guard, range extension through volume, voices following the listener, volumes and underwater filter.
- Music cycle: look-ahead bounds, a 20 s hitch, stop and fade, and the silence gap between pieces.
- AudioEngine: lazy unlock with state carried over, no-WebAudio no-op mode, a throwing context, playing while the first resume() is pending.

The whole repository suite (`node --test tests/*.test.js`) passes 324/324. `npm test` printed no output and exited 0 in this Git Bash shell, so I ran node directly.

Browser self-check: `node tools/harness.mjs --url "tools/audio-test.html?selfcheck=1" --wait-for "window.__audioCheck" --wait-timeout 200000` reports PASS with no page errors:
- All 70 sounds rendered offline through the full mixer: no clipping, none silent, no NaN. Loudest is the explosion at about −1.5 dBFS peak; quietest are steps at about −23 to −27 dBFS.
- A 28 s music excerpt renders with a −14 dBFS peak.
- The live AudioContext path passes: every sound plays, an 80-sound burst stays at 24 voices, a pig 30 blocks away is silent while an explosion there is audible, bad input never throws, and music starts in about 0.1 s and stops cleanly.
- `play()` costs about 0.11 ms per call on the main thread.

A separate harness run with real CDP mouse clicks confirmed: no AudioContext exists before the first click, the first click creates and runs it, the gesture listeners are then removed, and the positional map plays near sounds and drops far ones.

Screenshots were reviewed visually: spectrograms of every sound (stone, wood and metal were redesigned after this review), piano timbre, piano rolls of generated pieces, and the test page.
knownIssues: I could not listen in headless mode. Sound design was checked through spectrograms, waveforms and loudness measurements only; a listening pass may still want small level tweaks (`BLOCK_TRIM_DB`, `SOUNDS[name].gain`).
The sounds are synthesized approximations in Minecraft's character (crunchy stone, hollow wood, 'oof' hurt, moo, C418-style piano), not copies of Mojang's samples.
Moving sources keep their start position unless the caller updates them with the returned handle's `setPosition()` (useful for TNT and creepers).
There is no occlusion or cave reverb, just one global effects reverb (Minecraft has none either).
Pausing the game does not pause sounds or music; the hidden-tab suspend is the only automatic pause. game.js may call `stopMusic()` and `startMusic()` if it wants different behaviour.
In automation runs without a user gesture the engine stays silent by design. To exercise audio, call `__game.audio.unlock()` through harness `--eval`, which runs with `userGesture: true`.
The calibration gains are measured data: after changing a recipe, re-run `tools/audio-calibrate.mjs` (`import('/tools/audio-calibrate.mjs').then(m => m.run())` inside a harness eval).

report.summary:
The previous ENTITIES agent died from an API error during its final checks (about 02:59). Its owned files were already complete and wired by the integrator: spec 9.5 plus the F5 player model, falling sand, TNT and explosions, and entity save/load. This restart checked everything and then improved it.

Checks:
- 51 entity unit tests pass.
- Every view of tools/entity-test.html renders with no console errors (scene, item close-up, hand at 5 swing phases, 15 held items, 6 player-model poses, night, cave, torches/lava/drips, live simulation). Each screenshot was looked at.
- Real game (index.html?autostart=1&seed=42), driven by tools/out/ent2/real-steps.json with no console errors: drops of every kind rest on the ground, falling sand and gravel land, walking over the drops picked up all 46 items, three Q throws merged into one stack, F5 front view shows Steve holding the selected block, primed TNT flashes and explodes, the blast chain-primes a second TNT, and the crater has drops.

Changes this session:
1. Pickup fly-in now ends at the midpoint of the player's feet and eyes, as in Minecraft's ItemPickupParticle (was feet + 0.5); new test covers standing and sneaking.
2. Per-frame allocations. A new tool, tools/entities-alloc.mjs, uses V8's sampling heap profiler in Edge.
   - It first found the test page's fake world building string keys (fixed).
   - renderEntities: item, block and player instance matrices are written with inline math; stack-copy offsets are precomputed per item id; the frustum test is inline; uniforms are uploaded with uniform*fv from scratch arrays; plane extraction no longer uses Math.hypot; the player pose is computed at the origin with the camera offset added afterwards.
   - All 10 deterministic test views stay pixel-identical (0 pixels differ).
   - Root cause of the remaining reads: render objects started numeric fields as integer 0. The first fractional store changed their hidden class while the renderer was already reading them, so its property accesses went megamorphic and every double read allocated. Those fields now start as -0, giving exactly 3 stable hidden classes (item, block, model).
   - EntityManager.update now clamps dt with a conditional instead of Math.min.
   - Result: a test scene went from about 10 KB to about 3.5 KB per frame. A realistic manager-only scene (about 110 entities plus the player model, hand and particles) now allocates about 0.7–1 KB per frame in Edge, depending on JIT tier, plus about 135 B for the hand. Node shows about 10 B per frame.
   - Render CPU: 0.07 ms for about 500 entities, 0.45 ms for about 11,800.
3. The notes were rewritten to the final state: player model, ambient particles, allocation rules for wave 2, and the current integration including persistence.
apiDeviations: spawnItem returns null (no entity) for invalid input: missing stack, count <= 0, unknown item id, or non-finite position.
EntityRenderItem has three additive optional fields on 'item' and 'block': shadowY, shadow (alpha), shadowRadius. 'block' items keep their bottom at y when scaled, so primed TNT swells upward.

Additive 'model' kind { kind:'model', model:'player', x,y,z, bodyYaw, headYaw, headPitch, limbSwing, limbSwingAmount, attack, sneaking, age, hurt, death, light, itemId, shadow* }. EntityManager appends it (from PlayerAvatar) to getRenderList while game.perspective > 0. EntityRenderer.supportsPlayerModel = true.
Stack copies use Minecraft's getRenderAmount thresholds (up to 5 copies) instead of the spec's '1-2 extra copies'.
The pickup 'magnet' is Minecraft Java's ItemPickupParticle: the item flies to the player over 3 ticks after pickup. Items are not attracted before pickup.
Pickup reach is horizontal distance <= 1.5 from the player's axis, with the player box grown by 0.5 vertically.
Particles: layer 255 is procedural; u0 = style (0 smoke, 1 explosion, 2 droplet, 3 bubble, 4 flame, 5 lava pop, 6 drip, 7 speck), v0 = phase 0..1, uvSize = per-particle seed; light 255 = full bright.

spawnBlockHit takes an optional count (default 2). ParticleSystem constructor takes options { capacity, seed, ambient }. With game.player present, update() runs Minecraft's ambient display ticks: torch flames, lava pops, drips, underwater specks.
EntityRenderer constructor takes an optional third argument { textureData, layers }. Without it, sprite alpha comes from a one-time GPU read-back of the texture array.

Additive EntityManager APIs: list/entities, add, popItem, dropFromPlayer, spawnFallingBlock, spawnPrimedTnt, explode, anyEntityInBox, getEntitiesInBox, serialize/deserialize, avatar. getRenderList() with no argument returns a reused manager-owned array.
report.tests:
Unit tests: node --test tests/entities.test.js -> 51/51 pass (one test added: pickup fly-in path to the midpoint of feet and eyes).

Full suite: node --test tests/*.test.js -> 341/342. The single failure is the integrator's tests/game.test.js 'survival breaking drops an item that the player picks up'. It is flaky: about 30% of runs fail, and it passed in 4 of 6 isolated runs. A 2,000-drop simulation of the same setup (tools/out/ent2/pickup-sim.mjs) gives 71.7% pickup with the current entities.js and 71.3% with the previous attempt's copy. Each miss is a random pop velocity carrying the drop 1.6-2.2 blocks from a player who never moves, so this is not an entities regression.

Visual checks (harness screenshots, looked at, 0 console errors): tools/entity-test.html views scene / items / player / night / cave / ambient / handgrid / helditems / live. Pixel diff before and after the renderer refactor: 0 pixels differ in all 10 deterministic views (tools/out/ent2/base vs after and final).

Real game: tools/out/ent2/real-steps.json run through tools/harness.mjs on index.html?autostart=1&seed=42 -> no page errors.

Performance:
- tools/entities-bench.mjs (Node): EntityManager.update 0.31 ms for 1,000 falling items, 0.16 ms for 3,000 resting; particles 0.31 ms for a full 4,096 pool.
- window.__bench (Edge): render CPU 0.07 / 0.18 / 0.45 ms for about 500 / 3,900 / 11,800 entities.
- tools/entities-alloc.mjs: about 1-1.5 KB per frame total for the realistic scene (renderEntities about 0.7-1 KB).
knownIssues: tests/game.test.js 'survival breaking drops an item that the player picks up' (integrator's file) fails about 30% of runs. The block drop pops with a random velocity and can land outside the pickup reach of a player who never moves; Minecraft's own pickup box would miss most of these too. Suggested fix: walk the player onto the drop, or spawn the drop without random velocity.

Residual per-frame allocation in Edge: renderEntities about 0.7-1 KB per frame for about 110 entities, varying with JIT state and on-stack replacement (Node: about 10 B), plus about 135 B in the once-per-frame computeHandPose. Event-driven bursts such as block breaks and explosions allocate, as expected.

Items are not pushed by water currents; there is no flowing water until the wave-2 fluids/flowVector work. Liquids are detected with BLOCK.WATER and BLOCK.LAVA because the wave-2 liquid helpers (isWater, LIQUID_KIND) are not in the registry yet.
Entity shadows are one disc per entity at the receiving block's height (Minecraft clips per block). Translucent item cubes (ice, water) are blended without sorting.

Above 2,048 items, drops of the same item in the same 4x4x4 cell during one frame coalesce into one stack; beyond 6,000 items the oldest are discarded. This protects the frame rate from /fill ... destroy; no items are lost below 6,000.

The empty-hand arm and the third-person model use only the Steve skin. HandState carries no hurt tilt, so the first-person hand does not tilt when hurt (the camera does). The hand projection stays at fov 70 under water (Minecraft narrows it slightly).
report.integrationNotes:
Already wired by the integrator in src/game.js and verified this session. Construction: EntityManager(game) and ParticleSystem(game). The Renderer gets EntityRendererClass: EntityRenderer. World callbacks: onDropItem -> entities.popItem and onFallingBlock -> entities.spawnFallingBlock. Interaction uses spawnItem, dropFromPlayer, anyEntityInBox, spawnBlockBreak/Hit and spawnItemBreak; the player uses spawnBlockHit and spawnSplash. TNT goes through onInteractBlock -> spawnPrimedTnt. F5 uses game.perspective, and the 'model' render item is drawn by the EntityRenderer. Persistence: meta.entities = entities.serialize() and deserialize() after spawn placement.
